chapterTitle: Legal Aspects of the Safety Profession

questions.chapterTitle: Legal Aspects of the Safety Profession
questions.stem: A visitor sues after a fall in a known unguarded opening. Which set lists the core elements the plaintiff generally must establish for negligence?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A negligence claim generally requires a duty of care, breach of that duty, causal connection, and actual harm or damages.
incorrectOptionExplanations: These are criminal-process concepts and do not define negligence.
These facts may be relevant but are not the core negligence elements.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 2, torts and negligent torts, pp. 34-38

questions.chapterTitle: Legal Aspects of the Safety Profession
questions.stem: OSHA standards codified in the Code of Federal Regulations are primarily an example of what type of law?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Administrative agencies issue regulations under authority delegated by statutes, and those regulations are codified in the CFR.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Courts create and interpret case law, but OSHA standards are promulgated by an administrative agency under statutory authority.
A private contract does not create a federal regulation.
OSHA standards are not constitutional amendments.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 2, types of law and administrative law, pp. 33-34

questions.chapterTitle: Legal Aspects of the Safety Profession
questions.stem: Which situation most closely illustrates strict liability rather than ordinary negligence?
options: A driver runs a red light and causes a collision
A manager intentionally strikes an employee
A supplier fails to deliver goods under a contract
Harm resulting from an abnormally dangerous blasting activity even when reasonable care was used
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Strict liability can attach to specified abnormally dangerous activities or defective products without proving ordinary lack of reasonable care.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Running a red light is commonly analyzed as negligent conduct.
Intentional harmful contact is an intentional tort.
Failure to deliver is primarily a contract issue.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 2, strict liability and abnormally dangerous activities, pp. 38-40

questions.chapterTitle: Legal Aspects of the Safety Profession
questions.stem: An employee negligently injures a customer while performing assigned delivery duties. Which doctrine may make the employer responsible?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Vicarious liability can hold an employer responsible for employee conduct within the scope of employment even without direct employer negligence.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Stare decisis concerns adherence to legal precedent.
Assumption of risk is a possible defense and does not describe employer responsibility for employee conduct.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 2, vicarious liability and employer-employee examples, pp. 40-42

questions.chapterTitle: Legal Aspects of the Safety Profession
questions.stem: After a serious incident, litigation is reasonably anticipated. What is the strongest records practice?
options: Delete draft and unfavorable records immediately
Preserve relevant records and evidence under a controlled legal-hold process
Rewrite witness notes into one identical account
Continue normal automatic deletion without review
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Evidence should be preserved accurately, securely, and traceably when it may be relevant to a claim, investigation, or proceeding.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Destruction after litigation is anticipated can create serious legal and ethical consequences.
Independent observations should not be altered to create artificial consistency.
Routine deletion should be suspended for relevant information when a preservation duty arises.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 2, legal responsibilities and court process; Chapter 22, investigation records

questions.chapterTitle: Legal Aspects of the Safety Profession
options: Whether a court has authority to hear the type of dispute presented
How much insurance the defendant carries
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A court must have legal authority over the category of case, along with any other required jurisdiction and due-process conditions.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Jurisdiction is about authority to hear the case, not the merits.
Insurance may affect recovery but does not create subject-matter jurisdiction.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 2, court system and jurisdiction, pp. 29-33
